title: Lot Width From Area and Depth
description: Find a rectangular lot's width from its area and depth with Lot Width From Area and Depth — area ÷ depth, in feet, metres or acres. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a half-acre lot (21,780 sq ft) that runs 198 feet deep must be 110 feet wide — the frontage the listing forgot to mention, recovered by one division.
quick_answer: Lot Width From Area and Depth finds the missing side of a rectangular lot: width equals area divided by depth. Enter the area and the depth and read the width — the frontage figure that decides building envelopes and split feasibility.
steps_intro: Area ÷ depth = the frontage nobody printed:

body.t: Historic plats often state depth and area but let the frontage fade. The division restores it — and its twin restores depth:
Lot Depth From Area and Width
Zoning demands 75 ft of frontage per lot; the parcel computes to 110 ft wide — one lot, not two, whatever the owner's hopes. The width is where subdivision dreams meet arithmetic.
Frontage is value: retail and road-front parcels price by the front foot. A recovered width prices the access, not just the dirt.
Area, depth and width should multiply out. Run the solver on any two and compare with the third — the mismatch names the rounded (or invented) figure.
21,780 sq ft ÷ 198 ft deep = 110 ft wide. The 110 × 198 half-acre is a subdivision standard across the American Midwest — plat maps repeat it like a chorus.

A quarter acre (10,890 sq ft) at 217.8 ft deep implies a 50 ft width — a narrow, deep lot whose building envelope and price behave very differently from the 66 × 165 classic. The width is the character of the lot.

faq: Which side is 'width' on a corner lot?
Convention takes width along the addressed street. Corner lots can be read two ways — compute both and let the zoning code's definition of frontage settle which one governs.
Can I enter the area in acres?
Yes — acres, square feet and square metres all convert internally. Half an acre at 198 ft deep is the worked example on this page.
My lot tapers — front narrower than back.
Then two widths exist and the division returns their average. For pricing and envelopes, the front width is usually the binding one; measure it on the plat or the map.
The pole's width is access, not frontage in the usual sense, and the flag's width hides behind another lot. This solver prices the rectangular part; the pole is a legal conversation.
Width for a curved street frontage?
Chord versus arc: deeds usually state the chord or the arc length along the curve. The solver's straight width approximates both only for gentle curves.
How precise is the recovered width?
Exactly as precise as the area and depth fed in — a rounded 'half acre' (21,780 sq ft) hides ±hundreds of square feet, and the width inherits that fuzz proportionally.
Because depth and acreage sound generous and a 50 ft frontage does not. The solver exists so the omission never survives your due diligence.
